title: HelloHQ Plugin Manifest
description: One manifest.json per plugin lives at plugins/<id>/manifest.json. Validated by registry CI on every PR.

id.description: Reverse-domain identifier. Frozen at first submission. The 'hellohq.' prefix is reserved for Official plugins.

execution_mode.description: sidecar (Tier 1 Python) requires trust_tier: verified and is desktop-only.

content_hash_sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file at wasm_url. Verified by CI and by the app before every execution.

sidebar_icon.description: 24x24 single-fill SVG: an https URL, or for a webview plugin a path inside the UI bundle. An https icon needs sidebar_icon_hash_sha256. Invalid icons fall back to a generic glyph.

sidebar_icon_hash_sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the SVG served at an https sidebar_icon. The app downloads the icon once at install, checks this hash and draws the local copy; it never loads an unpinned icon from the network. CI verifies it, caps the file at 64 KiB and rejects scripts, foreignObject, event handlers and external references.

reason.description: One plain sentence shown to the person in the install dialog: why this plugin needs the permission. Optional; the host never uses it to decide anything.

allOf.$comment: propose:holdings / propose:valuations let a plugin SUGGEST a holding or a value that the person must approve in the app; they are Verified-only and require scope {"kinds": [...]} naming the asset kinds the plugin may propose. A missing scope is never read as 'any kind'. The kind enum is closed and MUST equal PluginProposePermission.kinds in HelloHQ/hellohq (lib/app/data/model/plugin/plugin_propose_scope.dart); hellohq has a test that compares the vendored copy of this schema with that set. The Verified-only tier check is in .github/workflows/validate.yml.

trust_tier.description: Assigned by the registry team at merge — do not set this yourself. Governs which capabilities the plugin may declare. community (default): Wasm-only, declarative/headless UI, no ai:inference, no write:external_output, no propose:*, no sidecar. verified: unlocks sidecar execution, ai:inference, write:external_output, propose:holdings, propose:valuations, and webview UI after manual Verified review. official: HelloHQ first-party plugins (hellohq.* id prefix).

provenance.description: Who built the plugin. 'core' is reserved for HelloHQ (requires an official signature) and is rejected from outside authors by CI. 'enterprise' is private to the org that built it and MUST NOT appear in the public registry — CI rejects it (see REVIEW_POLICY). Defaults to community.

licensing.description: Open-source vs commercial status. Surfaced as a badge in the in-app Plugin Browser so users see licensing before installing.

spdx.description: SPDX licence identifier for open-source plugins, e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0.

product_id.description: HelloHQ-brokered marketplace SKU. Required when kind == commercial.

publisher_signing_key_id.description: Assigned by the registry team at merge. Omit on first submission.

signatures.description: SA5: detached HYBRID publisher signatures, added by the registry signing pipeline after merge — do not set this yourself; omit on first submission. Each signature covers the artifact statement built by scripts/artifact-statement.mjs (plugin id, version, trust tier, execution mode, content_hash_sha256 and ui_bundle_hash_sha256), not the file itself: the app rebuilds that statement after checking the downloaded file against content_hash_sha256. A signed tier needs a valid Ed25519 AND a valid ML-DSA-65 signature from a trusted publisher key, fail-closed. Enforcement activates once the matching publisher keys are bundled in the app.

signature.description: Base64 detached signature over the artifact statement bytes.

allOf.$comment: read:aggregated_values requires an explicit portfolio scope.

network:fetch requires a non-empty origins allowlist on the permission scope. The app reads the allowlist from this scope (scope.origins), never from a top-level block. Entries are bare hostnames or a single-label wildcard (e.g. api.example.com, *.cdn.example.com) — no scheme, port, or path.
Commercial plugins must carry a HelloHQ-brokered marketplace SKU.
